# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s growth challenge is to turn advanced-model capability into dependable enterprise value through firms that influence buying decisions, design solutions, and carry implementation into complex customer environments.

This role is positioned where platform evolution meets partner execution. The key tension is making delivery patterns reusable without treating enterprise adoption as a one-size-fits-all exercise. Partners need clear technical guardrails,
practical learning paths, and credible escalation models; customers still need solutions adapted to their systems, controls, workflows, and change context.

The strongest operating model will preserve safety, product integrity, and customer trust while enabling external organizations to deliver with increasing confidence and independence.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation founded in 2021. Claude is its flagship model family, and the company describes its work through reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

The company combines frontier AI research with an expanding enterprise platform and ecosystem presence. Its commercial model depends on making sophisticated AI capabilities practical for organizations that must manage access, security,
administration, employee adoption, and production use.

Trust is central to the business proposition. Anthropic’s safety orientation is not simply a research message; it affects how customers evaluate risk, how partners frame deployments, and how the company protects long-term platform
credibility.

The operational challenge is to allow broad ecosystem participation while ensuring that implementation quality, responsible-use expectations, and customer experience remain coherent across varied cloud and delivery settings.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Enterprise AI adoption increasingly moves through cloud marketplaces, software platforms, consulting firms, and internal technology organizations. This makes an ecosystem-facing technical layer strategically important: it converts
product potential into credible customer pathways beyond direct engagement alone.

Claude serves multiple audiences, including enterprise users, application builders, and teams creating agents and applications. Those surfaces create varied routes to value, but they also raise the need for common technical patterns that
can be understood by administrators, developers, business owners, and delivery practitioners.

Partner scale brings a knowledge-management problem. Lessons from complex implementations must be converted into durable assets, training, architecture guidance, and product insight rather than remain attached to isolated accounts or
individual specialists.

Anthropic also faces a practical tradeoff between speed and consistency. Rapid market development can create uneven implementation practices unless partners receive enough structure to make sound choices without unnecessary dependence
on Anthropic personnel.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic’s public identity is closely connected to its founding emphasis on AI safety and societal benefit. That orientation makes technical quality, usage discipline, and clear customer communication important commercial concerns,
not merely compliance considerations.

Relevant stakeholder groups include:
- Enterprise platform teams responsible for administration, access management, governance, and the end-user experience.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as both an enterprise product and a developer platform. Its platform supports the creation of agents and applications, including managed agent infrastructure, which expands the architectural conversation from
interactive assistants toward integrated workflows and production applications.

Enterprise deployment guidance describes a connected journey spanning initial configuration, organizational launch, learning programs, and broader adoption. This indicates that the company views implementation as an organizational
capability-building effort, not solely a technical access decision.

That framing makes architecture work consequential beyond demonstrations. Effective designs must account for governance, user experience, operational ownership, evaluation, integration, and the mechanisms that help employees adopt new
ways of working.

Anthropic’s stated focus on reliability, interpretability, and steerability raises the bar for partner communication. Customers need deployment choices and product behavior explained in terms that support confidence in real operating
conditions, not abstract claims about AI safety.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly organizes its ecosystem across cloud, technology, and services partners. These categories play different but connected roles: cloud firms provide infrastructure and commercial routes; technology firms incorporate
Claude into broader offerings; services firms bring transformation and implementation expertise.

This is more than a referral model. The ecosystem must be able to identify suitable use cases, articulate technical feasibility, shape solutions with customer teams, and support adoption after an initial commercial decision.

Accenture publicly describes its relationship with Anthropic as combining enterprise AI models with industry and technology expertise to help organizations move faster with lower implementation risk. This illustrates a useful division
of labor: Anthropic provides model capability and platform direction, while delivery partners supply domain context, operating-model knowledge, and implementation capacity.

A scalable partner motion depends on practical shared assets: solution blueprints, enablement curricula, deployment checklists, technical communities, escalation pathways, and disciplined methods for collecting field insight.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public materials connect enterprise administration, organizational change, training, scaling usage, managed agent infrastructure, and partner participation. Together, these signals point to a market moment where
enterprise readiness must become repeatable across many delivery channels.

The urgency is not simply expanding the number of partners. It is ensuring that a growing ecosystem can create consistent customer outcomes before fragmented approaches, uneven quality, or unclear ownership patterns become entrenched.

As enterprise buyers move beyond experimentation, they expect providers and their delivery ecosystems to support governed workflows, integration decisions, user readiness, and measurable organizational value. Anthropic has an opportunity
to make Claude easier to operationalize while retaining the technical and safety standards that differentiate its platform.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building technical teams and operating rhythms that turn field learning into scalable assets.
- Connecting cloud, technology, and services ecosystems around coherent customer solution paths.
- Translating deployment friction and customer needs into structured product and engineering input.
- Communicating technical tradeoffs to senior business, partner, and engineering stakeholders.
- Making responsible AI practices concrete within enterprise implementation decisions.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise guidance connects technical setup with organizational launch, learning, and scaled usage.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, outcomes, scope, leadership, technical depth, and partnership experience must come from the governed resume/proof graph.

Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s growth challenge is to turn advanced-model capability into dependable enterprise value through firms that influence buying decisions, design solutions, and carry implementation into complex customer environments.

This role is positioned where platform evolution meets partner execution. The key tension is making delivery patterns reusable without treating enterprise adoption as a one-size-fits-all exercise. Partners need clear technical guardrails,
practical learning paths, and credible escalation models; customers still need solutions adapted to their systems, controls, workflows, and change context.

The strongest operating model will preserve safety, product integrity, and customer trust while enabling external organizations to deliver with increasing confidence and independence.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation founded in 2021. Claude is its flagship model family, and the company describes its work through reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

The company combines frontier AI research with an expanding enterprise platform and ecosystem presence. Its commercial model depends on making sophisticated AI capabilities practical for organizations that must manage access, security,
administration, employee adoption, and production use.

Trust is central to the business proposition. Anthropic’s safety orientation is not simply a research message; it affects how customers evaluate risk, how partners frame deployments, and how the company protects long-term platform
credibility.

The operational challenge is to allow broad ecosystem participation while ensuring that implementation quality, responsible-use expectations, and customer experience remain coherent across varied cloud and delivery settings.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Enterprise AI adoption increasingly moves through cloud marketplaces, software platforms, consulting firms, and internal technology organizations. This makes an ecosystem-facing technical layer strategically important: it converts
product potential into credible customer pathways beyond direct engagement alone.

Claude serves multiple audiences, including enterprise users, application builders, and teams creating agents and applications. Those surfaces create varied routes to value, but they also raise the need for common technical patterns that
can be understood by administrators, developers, business owners, and delivery practitioners.

Partner scale brings a knowledge-management problem. Lessons from complex implementations must be converted into durable assets, training, architecture guidance, and product insight rather than remain attached to isolated accounts or
individual specialists.

Anthropic also faces a practical tradeoff between speed and consistency. Rapid market development can create uneven implementation practices unless partners receive enough structure to make sound choices without unnecessary dependence
on Anthropic personnel.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic’s public identity is closely connected to its founding emphasis on AI safety and societal benefit. That orientation makes technical quality, usage discipline, and clear customer communication important commercial concerns,
not merely compliance considerations.

Relevant stakeholder groups include:
- Enterprise platform teams responsible for administration, access management, governance, and the end-user experience.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as both an enterprise product and a developer platform. Its platform supports the creation of agents and applications, including managed agent infrastructure, which expands the architectural conversation from
interactive assistants toward integrated workflows and production applications.

Enterprise deployment guidance describes a connected journey spanning initial configuration, organizational launch, learning programs, and broader adoption. This indicates that the company views implementation as an organizational
capability-building effort, not solely a technical access decision.

That framing makes architecture work consequential beyond demonstrations. Effective designs must account for governance, user experience, operational ownership, evaluation, integration, and the mechanisms that help employees adopt new
ways of working.

Anthropic’s stated focus on reliability, interpretability, and steerability raises the bar for partner communication. Customers need deployment choices and product behavior explained in terms that support confidence in real operating
conditions, not abstract claims about AI safety.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly organizes its ecosystem across cloud, technology, and services partners. These categories play different but connected roles: cloud firms provide infrastructure and commercial routes; technology firms incorporate
Claude into broader offerings; services firms bring transformation and implementation expertise.

This is more than a referral model. The ecosystem must be able to identify suitable use cases, articulate technical feasibility, shape solutions with customer teams, and support adoption after an initial commercial decision.

Accenture publicly describes its relationship with Anthropic as combining enterprise AI models with industry and technology expertise to help organizations move faster with lower implementation risk. This illustrates a useful division
of labor: Anthropic provides model capability and platform direction, while delivery partners supply domain context, operating-model knowledge, and implementation capacity.

A scalable partner motion depends on practical shared assets: solution blueprints, enablement curricula, deployment checklists, technical communities, escalation pathways, and disciplined methods for collecting field insight.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public materials connect enterprise administration, organizational change, training, scaling usage, managed agent infrastructure, and partner participation. Together, these signals point to a market moment where
enterprise readiness must become repeatable across many delivery channels.

The urgency is not simply expanding the number of partners. It is ensuring that a growing ecosystem can create consistent customer outcomes before fragmented approaches, uneven quality, or unclear ownership patterns become entrenched.

As enterprise buyers move beyond experimentation, they expect providers and their delivery ecosystems to support governed workflows, integration decisions, user readiness, and measurable organizational value. Anthropic has an opportunity
to make Claude easier to operationalize while retaining the technical and safety standards that differentiate its platform.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building technical teams and operating rhythms that turn field learning into scalable assets.
- Connecting cloud, technology, and services ecosystems around coherent customer solution paths.
- Translating deployment friction and customer needs into structured product and engineering input.
- Communicating technical tradeoffs to senior business, partner, and engineering stakeholders.
- Making responsible AI practices concrete within enterprise implementation decisions.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise guidance connects technical setup with organizational launch, learning, and scaled usage.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, outcomes, scope, leadership, technical depth, and partnership experience must come from the governed resume/proof graph.

- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.
